title: QUIC RFC 9000 Verifiable NEW_TOKEN Envelope
purpose: Describe the server-owned NEW_TOKEN envelope used to issue hard-to-guess, integrity-protected, IP-bound, expiring address-validation tokens and validate them before admitting future Initial packets.
design_summary: The listener owns an ephemeral address-validation token protector and passes the same protector to server runtimes it creates. Server NEW_TOKEN emission now asks the protector to issue a token for the validated remote IP address. The token carries an internal magic/version/source marker, a random nonce, issued and expiration timestamps, and an HMAC-SHA256 tag over those token fields plus the normalized client IP address. Future Initial packets with a non-Retry token are parsed before admission and validated with the listener-owned protector. A valid token pre-marks the runtime peer address as validated before the Initial datagram is routed to the connection; an invalid token is handled as unvalidated and, when Retry bootstrap is enabled, receives a Retry rather than address-validated admission.
data_and_state_considerations: The token secret is listener scoped and intentionally not persisted across listener lifetimes. The token does not store the client IP address in clear text; the IP address is bound through the integrity tag. Expiration uses wall-clock UTC timestamps because tokens can be consumed by a future connection rather than the issuing runtime's monotonic clock. Validation observations remain internal test-visible listener state and are not public API.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Tokens issued for the same address and timestamp remain distinct because each token includes a fresh random nonce.
Truncated, guessed, tampered, expired, and changed-IP tokens fail validation.
A valid NEW_TOKEN Initial bypasses Retry bootstrap and allows the server connection-options callback to run.
An invalid NEW_TOKEN Initial with Retry bootstrap enabled receives Retry and is not admitted as address validated.
alternatives_considered: Store every issued token server-side and compare opaque random bytes; rejected because it would not prove expiry or IP binding and would force stateful replay decisions into this prerequisite slice.
Embed the client IP address directly in the token; rejected because it exposes stable token contents unnecessarily and worsens observer-linkability risk.
Implement replay or one-time-use enforcement in the same slice; rejected because token reuse policy is owned by later S8P1P4 requirements and needs separate stateful design.
risks: Tokens are not valid across listener restarts because the secret is listener scoped.
This slice does not implement one-time token acceptance or replay limiting.
This slice does not claim observer-linkability closure beyond avoiding a clear-text IP address in the token envelope.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes the verifiable NEW_TOKEN prerequisite and first future-connection validation floor. Replay-limiting, one-time acceptance, token persistence across process lifetimes, and broader public token cache behavior remain out of scope.
